revelations.title: The witnesses carry questions, not answers
revelations.description: Free witnesses may question, compare, pause, propose language, and certify observed acts. They cannot answer for Tomas, Neris, a household, or an office they do not hold.

revelations.title: A year may be lost without a life being lost
revelations.description: Postponement loses the joining light for a year and carries real financial and public cost. It threatens no life and creates no supernatural penalty.

revelations.title: Marriage moves no deed
revelations.description: Marriage does not convey the mill, its debts, its succession, or the Concord water lease. Each remains with its own deed, office, and signatories.

revelations.title: The veil may shelter the living
revelations.description: Agnes's heirloom can honor Vale lineage and Perrin's memory as canopy, wrapping, threshold cloth, or another received use without covering Neris's face in river mourning dress.

revelations.title: Adoption adds duties, not ownership
revelations.description: Tomas may accept warning, evacuation, closure, rescue, and hearing duties, with reciprocal obligations from the river household, while remaining Vale kin and retaining property, residence, trade, refusal of unbounded danger, and every limit not expressly changed.

revelations.title: Care has names
revelations.description: Illness, incapacity, bereavement, and care for any future child belong to named people accepting named acts in an order. Marriage gives neither household default custody of spouse or child.

revelations.title: Iron promises only while open
revelations.description: Orren's labor can remain visible if the closed ring becomes a spiral, paired clasps, rush-gapped work, or threshold fitting. The correction honors the maker without asking Neris to wear captivity.

revelations.title: Ask where the feast came from
revelations.description: Hospitality begins by naming the food, its source, the taking it required, the person who prepared it, and the guest who freely receives it. “River fare” and “mortal fare” conceal too much.

revelations.title: Every gift declares its office
revelations.description: Before an object enters the ceremony, its giver states the honor offered and its receiver states the use accepted. The object may then be transformed, deferred, kept private, returned, or omitted.

revelations.title: Seat the guest, not the category
revelations.description: Menus, beds, chairs, routes, hearing, water access, participation, and abstention follow named guests and their choices. No household label supplies a body, appetite, or assent.

revelations.title: A vow must survive a changed course
revelations.description: Tomas and Neris must say what remains owed through changed residence, absence, work, grief, altered names, and possible separation. “While the river runs” is poetry until the next winter has duties.

revelations.title: The register can keep a name-chain
revelations.description: A stable witness identity can link Neris's changing bynames, parentage, and dwellings without replacing her current answered name or inventing a symmetrical river name for Tomas.

revelations.title: One rite may stand on wet and dry ground
revelations.description: Shallow moving rills, raised mats, dry turning spaces, and several linked sight lines let mortal and river guests witness the same acts without requiring the same footing.

revelations.title: The boat is a threshold
revelations.description: A stationary boat may receive Tomas into river kinship and return him to a chosen shared path. It need not carry him away, surrender the mill, or declare one household the sole destination.

revelations.title: Two tunes require two leaders
revelations.description: The procession works when each household audibly leads, answers, and joins. Simultaneous sound is insufficient if one rhythm remains the ceremony and the other becomes atmosphere.

revelations.title: A grievance names the next duty
revelations.description: The river custom records creditor, act owed, steward, and next hearing. It can be brief, bounded, partly private, and separated from attacks on character or demands for public reconciliation.

revelations.title: The rite must travel with the water
revelations.description: Consent, household standing, names, exchange, promises, and departure must survive a move among meadow, wheel yard, ford, willow bank, and shrine. One exact channel cannot carry the validity of the marriage.

revelations.title: The flood failed at the handoff
revelations.description: Agnes and Serein remember different true measures of Perrin's death. River signs, bell time, a lost route, and unassigned reception failed between the banks before Perrin chose to remain at the wheel.

revelations.title: Six acts carry the marriage
revelations.description: Consent, household standing, names, exchange, promises, and departure make the ceremony legible. Veil, ring, boat, music, dance, and response remain optional means whose office must be declared.

revelations.title: The folio may keep the disagreement
revelations.description: A valid record may preserve two household descriptions, an open clause, withheld recognition, or different signature scopes. Accuracy is stronger than a unanimity the participants did not give.

clues.title: The unsigned observation fields
clues.description: The folio has separate lines for each principal's repeated choice, every witness's observation, open clauses, abstentions, and certification scope. There is no line on which a relative or witness may answer for the couple.
clues.discovery: Lay the blank folio beside the commission before the final private repetition. Ask who owns each line and leave every unauthorized line empty.

clues.title: A pause without a placement
clues.description: During rehearsal, the commission lets the witnesses halt an unsafe or unintelligible sequence, but Agnes, Serein, Tomas, Neris, and every affected guest retain authority over their own place and participation.
clues.discovery: Read the operative verbs on the commission when the elders ask the party to assign precedence, apology, or joint testimony.

clues.title: The musicians’ unanswered question
clues.description: Iven asks whether the witnesses can order Moss to follow his count. The attached commission copy authorizes comparison and certification, not artistic or household command.
clues.discovery: Compare the witness seal with the authority described in the musicians’ work order.

clues.title: Reusable platforms
clues.description: Dessa’s modular platforms can be dismantled, stored, and raised next year; postponement wastes labor and goodwill but does not endanger the river or town.
clues.discovery: Ask Dessa what can be recovered if the ceremony does not occur this season.

clues.title: The joining-light calendar
clues.description: Ansel's calendar marks the single evening when wheel light reaches the willow threshold. It also lists ordinary dates on which Tomas and Neris could marry without the yearly spectacle.
clues.discovery: Set the gold joining-light mark beside the shrine's other valid wedding dates and ask what is lost at sunset—and what is not.

clues.title: Pella’s recoverable account
clues.description: Most food can be returned, redistributed, or preserved. The true costs of delay are money, travel, and public disappointment rather than starvation or supernatural reprisal.
clues.discovery: Have Pella separate recoverable stores from actual losses.

clues.title: The deed and lease books
clues.description: Mera sets four books on four corners of the table: deed, operating accounts, household entry, and Concord water lease. Different people sign them; different failures answer to different remedies.
clues.discovery: Have the witnesses carry each book to the person authorized to speak for it. No wedding sentence appears in all four.

clues.title: Separate certification lines
clues.description: The final folio records household standing, property, mill operation, water compliance, succession, and marital representation on separate lines; no marriage signature conveys all six.
clues.discovery: Read the separate lines aloud before the household-standing function and remove any broad formula that collapses them.

clues.title: The ford boundary stones
clues.description: Carved Vale boundary stones remain fixed while current marks pass through and beyond them; the rehearsal map must track property, water authority, and ceremony footing as overlapping but distinct claims.
clues.discovery: Walk the boundary with one reader of carved marks and one reader of water marks, then compare it with the household and lease clauses.

clues.title: The mill purse and the wedding purse
clues.description: Pella keeps the mill's grain account, Tomas's personal purse, and the household wedding fund on three separate hooks. The feast may spend from an authorized fund without merging the mill's ownership, debts, wages, or lease into the marriage.
clues.discovery: Ask who may authorize each purse, what each purse may buy, and whose obligation remains when one purse is empty.

clues.title: Shelter and mourning tunes
clues.description: Moss plays the river phrase for cloth over a face, then the phrase for cloth held above travelers in rain. The same flax enters the ear first as mourning, then as shelter.
clues.discovery: Ask Moss to play both uses before Agnes and Neris, then ask each woman which action she could receive without changing the other's intention.

clues.title: Canopy loops
clues.description: Dessa finds that the veil’s corner loops fit a light canopy frame without cutting or piercing the heirloom.
clues.discovery: Test Agnes’s veil against the reedwright’s frame.

clues.title: The open-door carving
clues.description: An old shrine carving shows a household cloth stretched over both spouses while their faces remain visible.
clues.discovery: Examine the weathered marriage panel beside the eastern doorway.

clues.title: The adopted wheelwright
clues.description: A former wheelwright carried a river adoption cord, answered warning and rescue calls, and retained his shop, surname, hill dwelling, and obligations to two mortal sisters.
clues.discovery: Read his maintenance and duty entries together in the mill’s oldest worker book.

clues.title: A prior dual-household compact
clues.description: A prior compact adds flood-watch and rescue duties to an adopted wheelwright while leaving surname, workshop, inheritance, burial, and mortal kinship untouched. Six limits are written in the same ink as six duties.
clues.discovery: Read one duty and its neighboring limit as a pair. Continue until Tomas can state both without Mera's help.

clues.title: The spoken limits of adoption
clues.description: The public adoption form pairs Tomas’s bounded duties with the river household’s reciprocal duties and names what does not transfer: Vale kinship, property, unrestricted labor, custody, or future children.
clues.discovery: Have Tomas and both household speakers paraphrase the duties, reciprocity, and limits before the ceremony begins.

clues.title: The cracked memorial bell
clues.description: The old flood bell is deliberately split so sound and water can pass through it; at rehearsal Orren can use its visible gap to correct an iron gift that appears closed from the audience angle.
clues.discovery: Compare the bell’s worked gap with the proposed iron from the witnesses’ actual position.

clues.title: The fiddler’s open clasp
clues.description: Iven's bow clasp is worked iron with an open mouth. It has held through twenty years of sweat and rain because the opening lets the leather be replaced.
clues.discovery: Let Orren handle the clasp and show how endurance can depend on an opening rather than a seal.

clues.title: Dessa’s rush-bound spiral
clues.description: Dessa can open the ring into a spiral and join its ends with replaceable rush, preserving Orren’s ironwork without closing metal around Neris.
clues.discovery: Have Dessa make a full-size mock-up before altering the ring.

clues.title: Orren's open-price sample
clues.description: Orren's market invoice includes a closed ring, an open spiral, and replaceable rush ties. The open version preserves his ironwork while allowing the fastening to be renewed or removed without cutting metal from the receiver.
clues.discovery: Compare Orren's sample, price line, and maintenance note before asking Neris which object and upkeep she would accept.

clues.title: The taking ledger
clues.description: The taking ledger records fish, mussels, reeds, herbs, and water by reach, season, permission, and keeper. No entry says merely “river food.”
clues.discovery: Choose one proposed dish and trace it backward through reach, taking, keeper, cook, and guest before it enters Pella's menu.

clues.title: The mill table
clues.description: River-adopted workers and mortal workers already share grain, mussels, and sea fish while refusing only food taken from a closed reach.
clues.discovery: Observe a mill meal and ask who supplied each dish.

clues.title: The source declaration form
clues.description: Mera’s feast appendix asks who grew, caught, traded, or released each course and what obligation follows.
clues.discovery: Inspect the source lines attached to the compact.

clues.title: The gift declaration
clues.description: At the exchange station, each giver must name the honor offered and each receiver the use accepted before the object moves. A mismatch leaves the gift in its custodian's hands.
clues.discovery: Rehearse the declaration with veil, iron, handstone, salt box, and cradle ribbon. Stop whenever the receiver answers a different question.

clues.title: The memorial bowl
clues.description: Agnes and Serein can use the same stone bowl in different memorial acts without conflict when each purpose is spoken and neither use is treated as the other woman’s assent.
clues.discovery: Hear each elder declare the intended use separately before deciding whether the bowl enters the ceremony.

clues.title: Two carved birds
clues.description: Iven and Moss received identical carved birds at prior weddings, once meaning departure and once return; context and declared use made the gifts legible.
clues.discovery: Compare the two musicians’ stories about the same symbol.

clues.title: Mara's gift inventory
clues.description: Mara's inventory names the handstone's owner, maker, intended honor, permitted alterations, and return if refused. Its proposed office is the base of a shared water bowl, not a title to Neris's labor or course.
clues.discovery: Set Mara's written intention beside Neris's paraphrase and change the public use until both sentences describe the same gift.

clues.title: The return-shelf register
clues.description: Ansel's register records a veil accepted as a canopy, a cup returned unopened, and a household token received in private. The marriages remained valid because the receiver's stated answer, not the object's mere appearance, completed each exchange.
clues.discovery: Read the giver's intention, the receiver's answer, and the final use as three separate lines in the shrine register.

clues.title: Pella’s service contracts
clues.description: Market contracts distinguish continuing duty, seasonal renewal, interruption, and release; Pella can paraphrase why one word cannot cover all four.
clues.discovery: Compare the musicians’ and caterers’ duration clauses.

clues.title: Neris’s private answer
clues.description: Away from both families, Neris says endurance must include changed channels, seasons apart, and a procedure for leaving without declaring the past false.
clues.discovery: Conduct Neris’s private consent interview.

clues.title: The bypass channel
clues.description: The bypass channel keeps water moving when the mill wheel stops. Tomas recognizes at once that continuity may require a changed route rather than unbroken motion.
clues.discovery: Walk the bypass with Tomas and ask him what a promise owes when the ordinary wheel cannot turn.

clues.title: The interrupted promise marker
clues.description: A rehearsal marker records the first wording of a promise, the changed route that interrupted it, the revised duty, and the people who accepted the revision. The obligation survives because its work can be restated, not because its first sentence is repeated unchanged.
clues.discovery: Move the promise station after water enters the route and ask Tomas or Neris to preserve the duty while changing the words or method.

clues.title: The House alias chain
clues.description: The House alias chain binds one stable witness mark to successive answered names, parentage, dwellings, and dates. Earlier names remain visible; none is overwritten as an error.
clues.discovery: Follow one person's chain across three bynames, then let Neris choose which parts identify her and which name the wedding will speak.

clues.title: Two columns on the final folio
clues.description: The name section separates stable witness identity, current answered name, parentage, byname history, dwellings, and household standing; later bynames append rather than overwrite.
clues.discovery: Ask Neris which form is spoken now, which changes may append later, and which replacement names she does not choose.

clues.title: Names across the flood deposition
clues.description: The old flood record follows Rain-at-Noon through an earlier byname by linking stable mark, parentage, and cross-reference rather than treating the witness as a different person.
clues.discovery: Compare the deposition heading, signature, and later cross-reference while preparing the final name folio.

clues.title: The shrine runnel
clues.description: The shrine’s narrow runnel crosses the open threshold, returns downhill through a screened outlet, and leaves enough dry turning space for benches and chairs.
clues.discovery: Measure the shrine runnel, return, and chair turning space against Dessa’s proposed aisle.

clues.title: The market fountain boards
clues.description: Market porters lay fountain boards so wheelchairs and dry shoes cross while a narrow ribbon of moving water remains open beside them. The arrangement already serves bodies that need different footing.
clues.discovery: Watch one market round. Mark where dry wheels, wet feet, carrying poles, and flowing water pass without ranking one route above another.

clues.title: Willow-root platforms
clues.description: The river household already uses low dry platforms above moving water for mortal guests and water-sensitive records.
clues.discovery: Ask how the existing platforms preserve both current and stable footing.

clues.title: The millhouse misunderstanding
clues.description: A Vale wall sketch labels the boat “Tomas departs,” revealing that the mortal family has inferred transport where no boatman or downstream route was planned.
clues.discovery: Compare the family sketch with the actual boat booking.

clues.title: The old adoption diagram
clues.description: An old adoption diagram shows a boat tied between two posts. The adoptee enters from one side, hears the duties, and steps out onto neutral ground; no journey follows.
clues.discovery: Trace the arrows with Tomas and Neris. Ask where the boat's office ends and who chooses the next path.

clues.title: The staged exit
clues.description: The final plan can have Tomas enter the stationary boat, hear and correct reciprocal duties, be received by Neris, and leave with her by the chosen shared route rather than being carried downstream.
clues.discovery: Walk entry, correction, dry bypass, and visible exit with the couple and boat steward before guests arrive.

clues.title: Pegging rhythm
clues.description: Dessa's crew pegs panels in four while passing lashings in six. Each pattern leads a different task; both arrive at the same tightened joint every twelve pulses.
clues.discovery: Listen through one complete module. Name the leader of each task and the point at which neither can finish without the other.

clues.title: The open-door response
clues.description: Ansel’s oldest response places a square spoken refrain and a lengthening sung answer in alternating leadership, with silence preserved for the consent question.
clues.discovery: Rehearse the response and identify who leads, answers, and holds silence at each cue.

clues.title: Fountain rounds
clues.description: Market sellers call prices in four while water carriers move in six around the fountain, producing an existing local pattern both households know.
clues.discovery: Observe one complete market round and mark where the calls and steps coincide.

clues.title: Moss's held entrance
clues.description: At the final joining measure, Iven reaches the shared pulse first. Moss holds silence until the river phrase's own lead cue, and the ceremony waits rather than treating his part as ornament beneath the fiddle.
clues.discovery: Watch who is permitted to restart the music after the consent silence and ask both musicians to name that authority aloud.

clues.title: The river obligation stones
clues.description: Serein's marked stones mean warning, repair, repayment, apology, and hearing. None means betrayal, selfishness, or bad blood.
clues.discovery: Have Rain-at-Noon enter the broken basket from creditor to stewarded close. Reject every sentence that describes Agnes instead of the work owed.

clues.title: Agnes’s basket debt
clues.description: Agnes can name a recent basket debt owed by Rain without reopening the flood quarrel, showing the custom’s ordinary practical scale.
clues.discovery: Ask Agnes what obligation Rain already acknowledged.

clues.title: Mera’s grievance ledger
clues.description: The House form records creditor, duty, next hearing, and steward; it has no field for attacks on character.
clues.discovery: Inspect a completed pre-feast grievance entry.

clues.title: The uncarried signal token
clues.description: A carved token marked 'mill gate received' remains unused in the old flood packet. The river watch had a duty to send warning, but nobody had accepted the matching duty to acknowledge, repeat, or escalate it.
clues.discovery: Place the unused token between Rain and Agnes and name the missing carrier, receiver, confirmation, and next act without naming a traitor.

clues.title: A tune with movable joining points
clues.description: Iven and Moss can preserve leadership, mandatory silences, and the twelve-pulse joining measure at bridge, ford, yard, willow bank, or shrine.
clues.discovery: Rehearse the same consent stop and departure joining at two acoustically different sites.

clues.title: Modular joints
clues.description: Every platform, rill tray, rail, and landing bears a relocation mark. The same six stations can be rebuilt at meadow, wheel yard, ford, or shrine before the marked deadline.
clues.discovery: Ask the crew to strip the plan to its fallback and carry one station to a second site. Note what meaning survives because it was not nailed to scenery.

clues.title: A site-independent rubric
clues.description: Ansel’s six-function checklist depends on witnessed acts, not a fixed bank, compass point, or water depth.
clues.discovery: Compare the officiant checklist with each fallback site map.

clues.title: The waterline after seating
clues.description: A fresh mud line crosses the planned aisle after the first guests sit. The marked stations can move one at a time while consent, household standing, names, exchange, promises, and departure remain observable.
clues.discovery: Compare the new waterline with the relocation marks and ask which function truly depends on the old position rather than on a visible act.

clues.title: Pella’s old delivery marks
clues.description: A surviving market delivery slate records two river warning signs before the mill bell rang, but no common conversion between those signs and bell time.
clues.discovery: Compare the slate’s water marks with the town bell notation.

clues.title: Rain’s borrowed bell
clues.description: Rain-at-Noon keeps the cracked handbell she carried during the flood because river signs alone did not make the Vales act.
clues.discovery: Ask why she kept a mortal bell after the water fell.

clues.title: The wheelhouse high-water cuts
clues.description: High-water cuts show danger reached the wheelhouse after earlier marks appeared outside. Perrin's abandoned tools show evacuation was still possible before he chose to save the wheel.
clues.discovery: Walk from the first cut to the gate and then to Perrin's tools. Put river mark, bell time, route loss, and personal choice in order without turning one into all four.

clues.title: The porter's unsigned wage slate
clues.description: A flood-year wage slate pays a porter to carry the first warning to the mill gate, but the receipt space is blank. The market can prove dispatch and route, not delivery, acknowledgment, escalation, or Perrin's later choice.
clues.discovery: Lay the wage slate beside Pella's water-mark delivery record and identify the exact point where evidence of a completed handoff disappears.

clues.title: Six rehearsal markers
clues.description: Six plain markers remain after children move decorations, rain turns the aisle, musicians stop, and every gift is removed: consent, household standing, names, exchange, promises, departure.
clues.discovery: Run the empty rehearsal and remove one prop at a time. If an act vanishes with its object, the act has not yet been designed.

clues.title: The procession’s six cues
clues.description: The score marks consent, household standing, names, exchange, promises, and departure, while leaving ring, veil, boat, dance, and congregational response optional.
clues.discovery: Compare each score cue with the couple’s selected act and identify where complete silence is required.

clues.title: Dessa’s function plan
clues.description: The platform drawing labels where each certifiable act can be seen rather than prescribing one inherited object.
clues.discovery: Read the sight-line annotations on the final construction plan.

clues.title: A respected open clause
clues.description: One respected compact sends an inheritance dispute to a later hearing under red cord. The marriage remained valid because the unresolved claim was named, bounded, and kept out of the ceremony's assent.
clues.discovery: Read the open clause and its later resolution. Ask what the earlier witnesses refused to claim on the wedding day.

clues.title: Abstention tokens
clues.description: Pella uses blank tokens for guests who attend but abstain from one course or custom, preserving presence without claiming participation.
clues.discovery: Inspect how abstentions are marked on the seating plan.

clues.title: A river compact with separate duties
clues.description: Serein’s archive includes kin who share rescue obligations while keeping separate property and burial customs; named difference did not weaken the bond.
clues.discovery: Review the compact’s explicit exclusions with Neris and Tomas.

clues.title: Two truthful menus
clues.description: Pella can place two truthful notes beside one meal: one names river permissions and returned obligations; the other names mill grain, paid labor, and household gifts. A single label reading 'our common feast' would claim more agreement than the cooks or guests made.
clues.discovery: Let Agnes and Rain strike only the sentence they cannot affirm, then preserve the shared operational list beneath both accounts.

clues.title: Mara’s named care instructions
clues.description: Mara's care instructions name Tomas, Agnes, and two neighbors in sequence for shelter, accounts, and guardianship. The phrase “Vale household” never appears where a person must act.
clues.discovery: Place the care instructions beside the deed and succession books. Ask Elsin which names she recognizes as promises and which pages merely describe property.

clues.title: The two-ledger care compact
clues.description: A prior mixed-household record enters a child in both a town register and river care ledger while assigning shelter, rescue, teaching, and notice to named adults and deferring permanent standing.
clues.discovery: Read the care signatures and the clause that neither ledger decides inheritance or residence.

clues.title: The unclaimed care lines
clues.description: The folio separates incapacity directions, survivor dwelling rights, and named care duties, then refuses automatic household custody; blank lines remain blank rather than being assigned to “both families.”
clues.discovery: Ask every proposed care signatory to state the exact act accepted before entering a name or leaving the clause open.

clues.title: The lifting rota
clues.description: Pella's seating rota names one person to steady Deep-Reed's chair, one to keep the shallow basin flowing, and one relief worker. No duty is assigned to 'the river household' or 'the Vales.'
clues.discovery: Remove one named worker from the rota and ask who notices, who substitutes, and who has authority to accept the replacement.

clues.title: The crossed-out household columns
clues.description: Mera has crossed out the columns marked VALE GUESTS and RIVER GUESTS. The replacement sheet asks for name, attendance, food, lodging, hearing, footing, water, gift, grievance, and abstention.
clues.discovery: Take one crossed-out total and rebuild it person by person until no accommodation belongs to a collective noun.

clues.title: Agnes’s corrected seat
clues.description: Agnes rejects the ceremonial “best elder place” and asks instead for a stable chair away from noise where she can see speakers’ faces.
clues.discovery: Ask Agnes where she can actually hear the vows and compare her answer with the seating label.

clues.title: Three incompatible river accommodations
clues.description: Deep-Reed needs a dry chair with moving water at her feet, Noll Ferry needs a dry bed, and Lilt-before-Storm needs audible current rather than wet lodging.
clues.discovery: Question the three guests together and record their distinct lodging and seating needs.

clues.title: The basin moved after the elder
clues.description: When rehearsal water reaches Deep-Reed's place, two helpers move her chair and leave the shallow moving basin behind. She stops them: dry support and current at her feet are one personal accommodation, not interchangeable signs of honor.
clues.discovery: Run the guest relocation once, then ask each affected guest which parts of their place must travel together and which may change.
